Rashi on Menachot 87b:11:1.english: And you would pose a problem for the Rabbis—for according to everyone, a half-tenth is required.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:12:1.hebrew: מדאמר ר"מ עשרון שבו מודד לחביתי כ"ג מחוק, חצי עשרון נמי מחוק הוה - דהא הוה נמי לחביתי כ"ג:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:12:1.english: From R. Meir's statement that the issaron in which he measured for the high priest's cakes was level - [we learn that] the half-issaron too was level, for it was also [used] for the high priest's cakes.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:12:2.hebrew: ומדר"מ - דאמר שניהם מחוק היו, אותו עשרון של כ"ג והחצי עשרון נמי. לרבנן נמי לא היה בו אלא עשרון אחד, ובו היה מודד לחביתי כ"ג, ה"נ דמחוק היה זה וזה, דלדברי הכל של כ"ג מחוק היה, דהכי פליגי בברייתא רבי מאיר ורבנן: מחוק שבו היה מודד לחביתי כ"ג, וחכמים אומרי' לא היה בו אלא עשרון אחד מחוק:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:12:2.english: And from Rabbi Meir - That is, [Rav Chisda] said: both were level-scraped - that tenth-vessel of the Kohen Gadol, and the half-tenth as well. According to the Rabbis too, there was only one vessel there, a tenth, with which he would measure for the Kohen Gadol's griddle-cakes; so too here, both this one and that one were level-scraped, for according to everyone the Kohen Gadol's vessel was level-scraped. For this is how Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis disagree in the beraita: [Rabbi Meir holds] it was the level-scraped vessel with which he would measure for the Kohen Gadol's griddle-cakes, while the Sages say there was only one level-scraped tenth-vessel there.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:14:1.english: The high priest's loaves: Those are the twelve loaves that he makes—six in the morning and six in the evening.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:14:2.hebrew: לחלות ביד או בכלי, ישער בידו או יחלקם בכלי:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:14:2.english: Into loaves by hand or in a vessel, whether by estimating by hand or by dividing them in a vessel

Rashi on Menachot 87b:14:3.english: Would he bring in tortni? - If he needed to bring in weights:

Rashi on Menachot 87b:15:1.english: Since it is written in a curse - "and they shall deliver your bread again by weight" (Leviticus 26).

Rashi on Menachot 87b:16:1.hebrew: שלחן מהו שיקדש קמצים בגודש שלו - כגון שאם הניח קומץ של מנחה או (של) לבונה בלא בזיכין שהיה לו לקדשו בכלי, והניחן על השולחן שבו לחם ולא קידשו בכלי אחר, והיינו בגודש שלו: שלא הניחו בבזיכין אלא למעלה בין לחם ללחם, שהכל היה בגודש, שלא הניחן בתוך כלי. ענין אחר בגודש שלו דשולחן לא היה לו בית קיבול כלל למעלה, וכל מה שמניחין עליו הוי כמו שמונח בגודש, כך שמעתי:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:16:1.english: How does the table sanctify handfuls by its heaping? - For example, if one placed a handful of meal-offering or frankincense without a vessel, though he was supposed to sanctify it in a vessel, and placed it on the table where there was bread and did not sanctify it in another vessel, then this is by its heaping: [meaning] he did not place it in a vessel but rather above, between bread and bread, [so that] all of it was in a heap, [meaning] he did not place it inside a vessel. Another explanation of 'by its heaping': the table had no receptacle at all on top, and anything placed upon it is [considered] as though it were placed in a heap, thus I have heard:

Rashi on Menachot 87b:16:2.english: That it is not fitting - for example, a handful and frankincense without vessels:

Rashi on Menachot 87b:17:1.english: It does not sanctify - for it is not its way to sanctify except for bread.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:17:2.hebrew: לדברי האומר טפחיים ומחצה קופל - כדאמרינן בפרק שתי הלחם (לקמן מנחות צו.) נותן ארכו של כל לחם שהוא עשרה טפחים כנגד רחבו של שולחן שהוא חמשה טפחים, נמצא ארכו של לחם יותר מרחבו של שולחן חמשה טפחים, נמצא קופל כל לחם ולחם טפחיים ומחצה מכאן וטפחיים ומחצה מכאן, נמצא ששה קיפולין של טפחיים ומחצה, שכל מערכה של ששה לחם גבוה חמש עשרה טפחים, נמצא השלחן מקדש חמש עשרה טפחים למעלה, כלומר דקידושו של שלחן היה עולה חמשה עשר טפחים, והיה מקדש כל דבר בין לחם בין קמצים בחמש עשרה טפחים דהיינו גודש שלו, ואמאי אמרת אינו מקדש:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:17:2.english: According to the one who says he folds two and a half handbreadths: As we say in the chapter "Two Loaves" (below, Menachot 96a), he places the length of each loaf, which is ten handbreadths, against the width of the table, which is five handbreadths; thus the length of the loaf exceeds the width of the table by five handbreadths. So each and every loaf is folded two and a half handbreadths on this side and two and a half handbreadths on that side, giving six folds of two and a half handbreadths [in a stack] - since each row of six loaves is [thereby] fifteen handbreadths high. Thus the table sanctifies fifteen handbreadths upward - meaning that the sanctifying power of the table would rise fifteen handbreadths, and it would sanctify anything, whether bread or handfuls [of frankincense], within fifteen handbreadths, which is the height of its heap. So why did you say it does not sanctify?

Rashi on Menachot 87b:18:1.hebrew: א"ל - הא דאמרי' אינו מקדש מאי דלא חזי ליה, היינו ליקרב, שאין הקומץ מתקדש שם שעדיין יש לו לקדשו בכלי אחר קודם שיקטירנו, אבל מקדש הקמצים ליפסל, דקדשי ליפסל בלינה וביוצא. עניין אחר מ"ר ז"ל: אבל מקדש ליפסל שפסולה המנחה, הואיל ועשאן שלא כמצותן, ושוב אין יכול להחזירן לעשרון:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:18:1.english: He said to him: What we say, that it does not sanctify whatever is not fit for it, means [not fit] for offering - that is, the handful (kometz) is not sanctified there [on the table], since it still needs to be sanctified in another vessel before it is burned. But it does sanctify the handfuls to become disqualified, for sanctified items become disqualified through being left overnight (linah) and through leaving the courtyard (yotzei). Another interpretation, from my teacher, of blessed memory: But "it sanctifies to become disqualified" means that the meal-offering becomes invalid, since he prepared them not in accordance with their law, and he can no longer return them to the tenth-ephah.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:1:1.hebrew: מחוק שבו היה מודד חביתי כ"ג - לפי שיש לו לחלק בשני חצאי עשרון, ואם היה גדוש, כשהיה מטלטלו לחצותו היה מתפזר על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:1:1.english: The level [tool] with which he would measure the griddle-cakes of the High Priest - Because he had to divide it into two half-tenths, and if it were heaped, when he would move it in order to divide it, it would scatter onto the ground.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:21:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק אומר - לא היה שם ד' מדות, אלא הין בלבד, ושנתות סימנין היו בו, עד כאן לפר כו', והכי נמי היו בו שנתות ללוג וחצי לוג: (*):(*)
Rashi on Menachot 87b:21:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Tzadok says: There were not four [separate] measures there, but rather the hin alone, and it had notches marking [the amounts], [reading] "up to here is for a bull," etc. And so too it had notches for a log and a half-log.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:22:1.hebrew: וכי מה היה הין משמש - והלא לא הוצרכו לו מעולם, אלא פעם אחת היה מימי משה לשמן המשחה, דכתיב שמן זית הין (שמות ל׳:כ״ד):
Rashi on Menachot 87b:22:1.english: And for what did the hin serve? - Indeed, they never needed it at all; rather, it was used once, in the days of Moses, for the anointing oil, as it is written: "a hin of olive oil" (Exodus 30:24).

Rashi on Menachot 87b:22:2.english: An additional measure - to complete the seven measures.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:22:3.hebrew: שבו היה מודד שמן לחביתי כהן גדול - שהיה צריכה שלשה לוגין, כדאמרינן לעיל (מנחות דף נא.), בשמן להוסיף לה שמן:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:22:3.english: With which he would measure oil for the griddle-cakes of the High Priest - For it required three log [of oil], as we say above (Menachot 51a), with regard to the oil, that oil was added to it [beyond the standard amount].

Rashi on Menachot 87b:23:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה קחשיב ממטה למעלה, ורבי מאיר קחשיב ממעלה למטה:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:23:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda reckons from the bottom upward, and Rabbi Meir reckons from the top downward.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:3:1.english: From the vav of the word “ve’issaron” [and a tenth], he derives it.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:5:1.hebrew: מנקודו - שאותו נקוד שעליו אתי למעט, דכל נקודה אתי למעוטי:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:5:1.english: From its dot - That dot which is upon it comes to exclude, for every dot comes to exclude.

Rashi on Menachot 87b:6:1.hebrew: שבו היה מודד חביתי כ"ג - השתא משמע שמודד חצי עשרון בביתו ומביא, והיינו דקא פריך מודד:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:6:1.english: With which he would measure the griddle-cakes of the High Priest - Now this implies that he would measure the half-tenth [of an ephah] at his home and then bring it; and this is what [the Gemara] challenges regarding [the word] "measures."

Rashi on Menachot 87b:8:1.hebrew: מחלק - שהיה מביאו מביתו שלם לעזרה, ואח"כ חוצהו בחצי העשרון:
Rashi on Menachot 87b:8:1.english: Dividing — that he would bring it from his house whole to the courtyard, and afterwards he would divide it by half-tenths.

Tosafot on Menachot 87b:14:1.hebrew: במה מחלקה לחלות - פירש בקונטרס שמחלקה לעיסה, וא"א לומר כך, דהא אמרינן לקמן (מנחות דף פח:) דרביעית נמשחה שבו היה מודד לחביתי כ"ג רביעית שמן לכל חלה וחלה, וקודם לישה צריך לבלול כשהוא סלת. ומכל מקום לא אפשר לעשות בו טורטני, דמשקולת ומאזנים סימן קללה בסלת כמו בעיסה, ומדה קטנה כל כך של א' משנים עשר בעשרון לא רצו לתקן, ואפשר דקטנה כל כך גם היא אינה סימן ברכה:
Tosafot on Menachot 87b:14:1.english: With what does he divide it into loaves? - Rashi explained that he divides it into dough [i.e., the division into the twelve loaves is done to the kneaded dough itself]. But it is impossible to say so, for we say further on (Menachot 88b) that the quarter-log [of oil] that was anointed was that with which he would measure the oil for the High Priest's griddle-cakes - a quarter-log of oil for each and every loaf - and this [measuring] must take place before the kneading, while it is still fine flour that needs to be mixed together [with the oil]. In any event, it is not possible to divide it precisely by weight, for a scale and balance are a sign of a curse when used with flour just as with dough. And they did not want to establish a measure as small as one-twelfth of a tenth [of an ephah, i.e., the portion per loaf]. And it is possible that something so small a measure is also not a sign of blessing.

Tosafot on Menachot 87b:16:1.hebrew: מהו שיקדש קמצים בגודש שלו - פי' בקונט': שני קומצי לבונה בלא בזיכין. וקשיא, דהוה ליה למימר לבונה בהדיא. ועוד, כיון דעם שולחן נמי בעי בזיכין, כדכתיב "כפותיו", ותניא לקמן בפרק שתי הלחם (מנחות דף צז.): "כפותיו" אלו הבזיכין - היאך תיסק אדעתין למימר דסגי בלא בזיכין? ונראה לפרש דמיירי בקומץ של מנחה, כדאמרי' בפ"ק (לעיל מנחות ח.) דמנח' שקמצה בהיכל כשרה. ומיהו הא דמסיק: "אינו מקדש ליקרב אבל מקדש ליפסל" - לפי' הקונטרס ניחא, דמקדש ליפסל בטבול יום ובלינה, דאי לאו שולחן לא מיפסלי, דעדיין לא נתקדשה בכלי שרת כיון דלא נתנוה בבזיכין. אבל למאי דפרישית, הא מיקמי הכי כבר נתקדשה כולה מנחה בכלי שרת, ומיפסלא בטבול יום ובלינה. ויש לפרש כי ההוא דפ"ק (שם ו:) גבי זר שקמץ דמקדשין ליפסל, לענין דלא מהני תו חזרה מאחר שנתקדש הקומץ על השולחן:
Tosafot on Menachot 87b:16:1.english: What is the halakha as to whether it consecrates handfuls on its heaped upper part - Rashi explains: the two handfuls of frankincense [that accompany the showbread], without their dishes (bazichin). But this is difficult: it should have said "frankincense" explicitly [rather than the more general "handfuls"]. And furthermore, since the Table itself requires dishes - as it is written, "kapotav" (its ladles) - and it was taught below, in the chapter "Shtei HaLechem" (Menachot 97a): "kapotav" - these are the dishes (bazichin) - how could it enter our minds to say that it would suffice without the dishes? It therefore seems that the explanation is that this is discussing the handful (kometz) of an ordinary meal-offering, as we say in the first chapter (above, Menachot 8a), that a meal-offering whose handful was removed in the Sanctuary hall [rather than on the Table] is valid. However, that which the Gemara concludes - "it does not consecrate it so that it may be offered up, but it does consecrate it so that it becomes disqualified" - works out well according to Rashi's explanation: it consecrates it so that it becomes disqualified through [contact with] one who immersed that day and through being left overnight, for if not for the Table, they would not become disqualified, since it had not yet been consecrated in a service vessel, seeing as they had not placed it in the dishes. But according to what I have explained, this is difficult: for even before this, the entire meal-offering had already been consecrated in a service vessel [when the handful was removed], and so it would already become disqualified through being touched by one who immersed that day and through being left overnight, [regardless of the Table]. It is therefore possible to explain that this is like that case in the first chapter (there, 6b), regarding a non-priest who performed the handful-removal, that it "consecrates so that it becomes disqualified" - meaning that, in that regard, going back [to redo the removal properly] no longer helps, once the handful has been consecrated on the Table.

Tosafot on Menachot 87b:21:1.hebrew: שנתות היו בהין - בפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף פו:) אמרי': כדאמר רב כהנא "שנתות היו בהין", ה"נ "שנתות היו במדות". ופירש שם רבינו שמואל, דמילתא דרב כהנא בפ' שתי מדות ואינה כאן, אלא משנה שלימה שנינו. אבל במסכת שבת פרק המוציא יין (שבת דף פ:) גבי אנדיפי מפרש רב כהנא שנתות, כדתנן "שנתות היו בהין". והשתא הכי קאמרינן התם: כדאמר רב כהנא על תירוץ אחר "שנתות היו בהין", הכא נמי נתרץ "שנתות היו במדות":
Tosafot on Menachot 87b:21:1.english: There were notches in the hin - In the chapter "One Who Sells a Ship" (Bava Batra 86b) they say: just as Rav Kahana said, "There were notches in the hin," so too here [we may say], "There were notches in the measures." And Rabbeinu Shmuel explained there that Rav Kahana's statement actually belongs in the chapter "Shtei Middot" [i.e., here, in this chapter of Menachot], and is not truly [said] there [in Bava Batra] - rather, there they cited a complete mishnah [as a proof-text, not Rav Kahana's own words]. But in tractate Shabbat, in the chapter "One Who Carries Out Wine" (Shabbat 80b), regarding andifei, Rav Kahana himself explains "notches" in accordance with what we learned: "There were notches in the hin." And now, this is what we mean when we say there [in Bava Batra]: just as Rav Kahana said - in the context of a different answer - "There were notches in the hin," so too here let us answer, "There were notches in the measures."

Tosafot on Menachot 87b:7:1.hebrew: מודד ורמינהו חביתי כהן גדול כו' - מהא דקאמר ר"מ: ומחוק שבו מודד לחביתי כ"ג, לא בעי לאקשויי, דסלקא דעתך שפעמים מודד בזה ופעמים בזה:
Tosafot on Menachot 87b:7:1.english: Does he measure? But we raise a contradiction: the High Priest's griddle-cakes, etc. - There is no need to raise a difficulty from that which Rabbi Meir said [in the mishna], 'and the leveled one is that with which he measures for the High Priest's griddle-cakes' [implying that it is the whole, level tenth-measure that is used] - for one might have said that sometimes he measures with this vessel and sometimes with that one, [so Rabbi Meir's two statements are not truly contradictory, and the Gemara therefore needed to bring the explicit teaching that the griddle-cakes are never brought in halves].
